scylla: Scylla, -ae (f.) — Scylla, the sea-monster of the strait (nom. sg.)
sede: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, site (abl. sg.)
sedet: sedeō, sedēre, sēdī — to sit (3rd sg. pres.) · also impers., it is fixed, resolved (+ dat.)
sensus: sēnsus, -ūs (m.) — feeling, sense, emotion, mind (nom. sg.; acc. pl.)
sequi: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue (pres. inf., deponent)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
siculo: Siculus, -a, -um — Sicilian, of Sicily (n./m. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sinum: sinus, -ūs (m.) — fold of a garment, bosom, lap (acc. sg.)
stetit: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd sg. perf.)
stirpem: stirps, stirpis (f.) — stock, root, stem; lineage, race (acc. sg.)
sublapsa: sublābor, -ī, -lapsus sum — to slip away, sink down (perf. part., f. nom. sg., deponent)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
suorum: suus, -a, -um — his, her, their own; suī (m. pl.) one's own people (m. gen. pl.; also n. gen. pl.)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō)
superos: superī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the gods above (acc. pl.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tam: tam (adv.) — so, so much, to such a degree
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tantis: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
tenebris: tenebrae, -ārum (f. pl.) — darkness, gloom, shadows (abl./dat. pl.)
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
teucrum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Teucrians, Trojans (gen. pl., archaic -um for -ōrum)
thybridis: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (gen. sg., Greek form)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
totiens: totiēns (adv.) — so often, so many times
tristia: tristis, -e — grim, sad, bitter (n. acc. pl.)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
troianas: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. acc. pl.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuorum: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.); tuōrum, of your people (m. gen. pl.)
tyranni: tyrannus, -ī (m.) — ruler, despot, tyrant (gen. sg.) · also m. nom. pl. (tyrannī, the rulers)
udo: ūdus, -a, -um — wet, moist, sodden (m./n. abl. sg.)
unum: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single, the same (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
usque: usque (adv.) — all the way, continuously, ever, without ceasing
valuit: valeō, -ēre, valuī — to be strong, be able, prevail (3rd sg. perf.)
vasta: vastus, -a, -um — vast, huge, desolate (f. abl. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
velit: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want, be willing (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
venenis: venēnum, -ī (n.) — drug, potion, poison; magic juice (abl./dat. pl.)
veneri: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love (dat. sg.)
versare: versō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to turn over, turn about, ply, contrive (pres. inf.)
verti: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, overturn (pres. pass. inf.)
vertit: vertō, vertere, vertī, versum — to turn, change (3rd sg. pres./perf.)
vexit: vehō, -ere, vēxī, vectum — to carry, convey, bear along (3rd sg. perf.)
videt: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. pres.)
vires: vīs (f.) — force; pl. vīrēs, strength (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (fractae vīrēs)
volvitur: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, tumble (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
